answer: An agent economy can resist a gale of fake identities by anchoring each identity to marble-slow local reputation: an agent must complete real errands for distinct residents of one neighborhood over weeks, with residents rating the work and staking deposits they lose for false vouches. One operator cannot staff many neighborhoods at once, and each further identity on the same funding trail pays a deposit doubling the last, so every extra fake costs another local runner, another set of real residents, and twice the prior deposit. No ivory-tower shortcut of bought ratings survives a slash.
